# levelgx

> Inspect game levels for reachability, solvability and soft-locks. Reports problems with stable codes and exit codes, and writes an annotated storyboard.

levelgx is one of the `gxkit` agent-native review tools. A level is a grid of
characters; `levelgx inspect` flood-fills from the spawn, proves the goal is
solvable, finds stranded items, and catches soft-locks caused by one-way tiles.

## Install

```sh
uvx --from "git+https://github.com/nekomario28/gxkit#subdirectory=packages/levelgx" levelgx --help
uv tool install ./packages/levelgx      # from a clone
```

Needs Python 3.10+ and Pillow.

## Use

```sh
levelgx inspect level.py            # report + storyboard, exit 1 on any error
levelgx inspect level.py --json
levelgx inspect level.py --no-storyboard
levelgx render  level.py -o level.png
```

A level file defines `rows` (a list of strings), `LEVEL`, `level` (a `Level`),
or a `build()` returning one.

## The legend

`#` wall · `.` floor · `S` spawn · `G` goal · `X` item · `!` hazard ·
`>` `<` `^` `v` one-way tiles.

## Checks

error: `no-spawn`, `no-goal`, `goal-unreachable`, `soft-lock`, `stranded-item`.
warn: `hazard-cuts-off`.
info: `unreachable-area`, `no-items`.

Full documentation is in `README.md`.
